findings: non-blocking: reckon/crew/promotion.py:296 the retirement compares only the four fields pointer_attempt returns (attempt, phase, pid, pid_start_time) against the promotion's own record, while the owner of this capability, _remove_promoted_pointer at reckon/crew/promotion.py:231-247, compares fourteen fields including resume_launch_in_flight, worktree, log_path and backend; a pointer that differs only in those fields is therefore removed where the owner refuses, so the repository now holds two different answers to 'has this pointer moved'.

non-blocking: reckon/crew/promotion.py:321 the review branch now returns the retirement's boolean, and both call sites discard it (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1478 and :2155), so a promotion that has just concluded a pointer belongs to a newer attempt still proceeds into _release_after_promotion at reckon/crew/promotion.py:1484-1489; that release builds its live-pointer claims at reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:449 with `if claim != run_id`, excluding the run's own id, so the in-flight attempt's own worktree is not protected by its surviving pointer, and tests/test_promoted_review_never_held_for_landing_repair.py:166-176 asserts only that the pointer survived, never that the workspace did.

non-blocking: tests/test_promoted_review_never_held_for_landing_repair.py:175-176 assert kept['attempt'] == 2 and kept['phase'] == 'running', both values the test itself wrote at :147-148, so either would hold for any code that leaves the file untouched; the independent guard in that test is the read_pointer call at :174, which raises CrewError and reddens the test if the pointer is unlinked.
